question: What's the name of the misfit elf who ditches Santa's workshop to run off with Rudolph?
hint: Rhymes with “germy.” Wants to fix teeth, not toys. Elf HR is concerned.
funFact: His voice, Paul Soles, went on to voice Peter Parker in the 1967 Spider-Man cartoon. From elf dentist to web-slinger!

question: What's the name of the loud, bushy-bearded prospector who joins Rudolph's road trip?
hint: First name: a chilly Canadian territory. Personality: a one-man avalanche.
funFact: Voice actor Larry D. Mann was one of many Canadians in the cast, which recorded its lines in Toronto. No wonder he loves a blizzard.

question: What does Rudolph's dad make him wear to hide that glowing red nose? (Parenting tip: don't.)
hint: A cover-up job. It pops right off at the Reindeer Games.
funFact: Believe it or not, this was the UPGRADE: before that, his dad tried covering the nose with mud.

question: What's the name of the friendly, umbrella-toting snowman who narrates the special?
hint: Three letters. He'd look great in a star-spangled top hat as Uncle ___.
funFact: He's voiced by folk singer Burl Ives, a late addition to please NBC and sponsor General Electric. A snowman brought to you by GE!

question: Finish Santa's big request on that foggy Christmas Eve: “Rudolph, with your nose so bright…”
answer: Won't you guide my sleigh tonight?
accept: Will you guide my sleigh tonight
hint: Santa needs a GPS. Rudolph IS the GPS.
funFact: Rudolph's reply: “It will be an honor, sir.” Somewhere, every reindeer who laughed at him felt VERY awkward.

question: Which young doe tells Rudolph he's cute, making him so giddy he literally takes off?
hint: Her name rhymes with “police.” She thinks the nose is cute, and she's right.
funFact: She later sings him the gentle ballad “There's Always Tomorrow.” Smooth, Clarice. Very smooth.

question: Who said it? “Whoever heard of a skinny Santa?”
hint: She runs the North Pole kitchen, the calendar and possibly the whole operation.
funFact: Plot twist: the famous combo “Eat, Papa, eat. Nobody likes a skinny Santa” is a misquote. Nobody says that exact line!

movie: Santa Claus Is Comin' to Town (1970)
question: What's the name of Sombertown's grumpy, toy-hating mayor? (Bonus points for saying it three times fast.)
hint: His name is a mouthful: like ordering a burger, then the same burger backwards.
funFact: Voice actor Paul Frees plays him, both Kringle brothers AND a crowd of townsfolk and soldiers. Busiest guy in Sombertown.

movie: Santa Claus Is Comin' to Town (1970)
question: What kind of animal is Topper, the tiny tagalong Kris meets on his way to Sombertown?
hint: A flightless bird that's always dressed for a fancy dinner party.
funFact: Kris later marries the schoolteacher Jessica, who becomes Mrs. Claus. A love story AND a tiny tuxedo bird: this special has it all.

question: How much does Lucy charge at her “Psychiatric Help” booth? (Cheapest therapy in history.)
hint: Less than a dime, and she still makes Charlie Brown pay up front.
funFact: The Doctor is IN, and has been since 1959, when Lucy's advice booth first opened in the Peanuts comic strip.

question: What does Snoopy deck out to win the neighborhood lights and display contest?
hint: It's his house, technically. He sleeps on the ROOF of it.
funFact: Charlie Brown is crushed: even his own dog has gone commercial. Snoopy: zero regrets, one trophy.

question: The gang wants a big, shiny aluminum tree. What does Charlie Brown drag home instead?
hint: Hang ONE ornament on it and the whole thing flops over.
funFact: Lucy's actual order: “Get the biggest aluminum tree you can find, Charlie Brown, maybe painted pink.” He did not.

question: Finish the lyric: “You're as cuddly as a cactus, you're as charming as an…”
hint: A slippery, snake-shaped fish you would NOT want to hug.
funFact: It's sung by Thurl Ravenscroft, the voice of Frosted Flakes' Tony the Tiger. The Grinch? He's NOT grrreat!

question: At the Whos' feast at the end, what does the reformed Grinch get the honor of carving?
hint: It rhymes with “feast” and sounds like a monster you'd find under the bed.
funFact: He hands the very first slice to his faithful dog, Max. Honestly, Max deserved the WHOLE thing.

question: Who plays the Grinch, green fur and all, in Ron Howard's 2000 live-action movie?
hint: The rubber-faced star of The Mask and Ace Ventura. Alrighty then!
funFact: The makeup was so grueling that producers hired a former Navy SEAL commander, an expert at teaching people to endure torture, to coach him through it.

question: What does the Pumpkin King keep mistakenly calling Santa Claus?
hint: Sounds like a day at the beach plus a lobster's pincers.
funFact: He even asks Sally to sew him a Santa suit. Fashion news: skeletons look great in red.

question: Finish Jack's wide-eyed opening line of the song “What's This?”: “What's this? What's this? There's color…”
hint: All over the place. On every single thing. Jack is OVERWHELMED.
funFact: It was the first animated film ever nominated for the Best Visual Effects Oscar. Not bad for a bunch of skeletons.

question: Santa lets the boy choose the first gift of Christmas. What does he pick?
accept: A bell from a reindeer's harness
hint: It rings, but only for believers. Grown-ups hear nothing.
funFact: By the end, even his sister Sarah can no longer hear it ring. Moral: keep believing, or enjoy a very quiet souvenir.

question: On the way north, a gigantic herd blocks the tracks. What animals cause this holiday traffic jam?
hint: Santa's wild cousins: antlers, hooves and zero respect for train schedules.
funFact: To clear them, the Conductor yanks engineer Smokey's beard, and Smokey's yelp gets the herd moving. Beard-powered pest control!

question: Who plays George Bailey, the man who gets a guided tour of life without him?
hint: He also starred in Vertigo and Mr. Smith Goes to Washington. Famous drawl, famous Jimmy.
funFact: It was his first film after flying bombers in World War II. Saving Bedford Falls was the easy part.

question: Finish George's smooth-talking offer to Mary: “You want the moon? Just say the word, and I'll throw a…”
answer: Lasso around it and pull it down
hint: A cowboy's rope trick, aimed at outer space.
funFact: On that same walk they throw rocks at the old Granville house to make wishes, and it later becomes their home. Wish: granted.

question: When George gets his life back, what tiny treasure turns up in his pocket?
hint: Something from his little daughter's flower, which he'd tried to fix.
funFact: His whole crisis began when Uncle Billy misplaced $8,000 of the Building and Loan's money. Uncle Billy: never in charge of deposits again.

question: What does little Susan ask Kris to get her for Christmas? (Not a doll. Not a bike. Think BIGGER.)
hint: She tore its picture out of a magazine. It comes with a backyard.
funFact: In the final scene, Fred and Doris find a cane just like Kris's in that very house. Cue the goosebumps.

question: How does lawyer Fred Gailey finally prove in court that Kris is the one and only Santa Claus?
answer: The Post Office delivers Santa's letters to Kris
accept: Mail to Santa delivered to him
hint: The government gets involved: bags and bags of evidence, special delivery.
funFact: Fox released this Christmas movie in early summer 1947 and kept Christmas out of the ads. Surprise, it's Santa!

question: In Home Alone, finish the gangster's line from the old movie Kevin watches: “Keep the change…”
hint: A very rude way to say thanks for the pizza.
funFact: Kevin plays the scene on his VCR to scare off the Little Nero's pizza guy. Worst tip ever, best prank ever.

question: In Home Alone, what creepy-crawly pet does Kevin's big brother Buzz keep in his room?
hint: Eight hairy legs. Zero chill.
funFact: Yes, it's a REAL tarantula on Marv's face. Daniel Stern had to mime his scream so he wouldn't spook the spider; the sound was added later.

question: In Home Alone's most famous scene, what does Kevin slap on his cheeks right before he screams?
hint: It's from Dad's side of the bathroom, and it STINGS.
funFact: Macaulay Culkin was told to pull his hands away before screaming. He kept them on his cheeks, and that take became iconic.

movie: Home Alone 2: Lost in New York (1992)
question: In Home Alone 2, Kevin ends up in New York. Where is the rest of the McCallister family spending Christmas?
hint: Sunshine, palm trees and beaches. Kevin got the snow; they got the sunscreen.
funFact: This time nobody leaves him at home: he follows a man in his dad's coat onto the wrong plane. Progress?

movie: Home Alone 2: Lost in New York (1992)
question: In Home Alone 2, which fancy New York hotel does Kevin check into using his dad's credit card?
hint: It overlooks Central Park, and its name is also a word for a town square.
funFact: The suspicious concierge is Tim Curry, the frantic butler from Clue. Nobody suspects a 10-year-old. Except him.

question: In Elf, finish Buddy's advice to Jovie: “The best way to spread Christmas cheer is…”
answer: Singing loud for all to hear
accept: Singing loudly for all to hear
hint: Do it loudly, in front of everyone. And it rhymes with “cheer.”
funFact: At the end, Jovie gets a whole crowd singing “Santa Claus Is Comin' to Town” to power Santa's sleigh. Advice: taken.

question: In Elf, Buddy bursts into a little New York diner to congratulate them on having the world's best… what?
hint: A hot drink. The sign said “world's best,” and Buddy believes every sign.
funFact: Spot the cameo: Peter Billingsley, Ralphie from A Christmas Story, plays Ming Ming, an elf at the North Pole.

question: In Elf, a snowball smacks Buddy right in the face. Finish his yelp: “Ow! Son of a…”
hint: A wooden soldier with a big jaw and a serious walnut habit.
funFact: Buddy then single-handedly wins the snowball fight for his half brother, Michael. North Pole training is no joke.

question: In Christmas Vacation, Clark finds the perfect tree out in the country. What essential item did he forget?
accept: Something to cut it down with
hint: It has a jagged blade and would have been VERY handy.
funFact: The film skips the digging: next shot, the tree is strapped to the car, roots and all. Clark Griswold does not do small.

question: In Christmas Vacation, what critter leaps out of the Griswolds' Christmas tree and causes total chaos?
hint: Bushy tail, loves nuts, came free with the tree.
funFact: Christmas Vacation was written by John Hughes, who wrote Home Alone a year later. The man loved a holiday disaster.

question: In Christmas Vacation, sweet Aunt Bethany is asked to say grace. What does she recite instead?
hint: Schoolkids say it every morning, hand on heart, facing the flag.
funFact: Aunt Bethany is Mae Questel, the longtime voice of Betty Boop and Olive Oyl. Boop-oop-a-doop!

question: In A Christmas Story, Flick takes a dare at school. What gets stuck to the frozen flagpole?
hint: Open wide and say “ahh”… then do NOT touch the metal.
funFact: No tongues were harmed: the pole was sheathed in plastic, and a hidden suction tube held the tongue in place.

question: In A Christmas Story, the Old Man reads FRAGILE on a crate as “Fra-gee-lay.” What does he decide it must be?
hint: Think pizza, pasta and gondolas. Mamma mia!
funFact: Inside the crate: the infamous leg lamp, the Old Man's “major award.” Mother was… less impressed.

question: In A Christmas Story, what gloriously embarrassing gift does Aunt Clara send Ralphie?
hint: Long floppy ears, a fluffy tail and zero dignity.
funFact: The Old Man's verdict: Ralphie looks like “a deranged Easter Bunny.” Aunt Clara meant well!

question: In Die Hard, McClane hides by crawling through what part of the building, joking, “Now I know what a TV dinner feels like”?
hint: A cramped metal tunnel behind the ceiling grilles. Snug fit, zero legroom.
funFact: Die Hard hit theaters in July 1988, which fuels the yearly “Is it a Christmas movie?” family debate. Discuss. Loudly.

question: In The Santa Clause, Scott Calvin startles Santa on Christmas Eve. What does Santa tumble off?
hint: It's where a sleigh parks. Do not try this at home.
funFact: Soon Scott's hair turns white and he grows a beard he can't shave off. Always read the fine print!

question: In The Santa Clause, after Scott burns the turkey, where do he and Charlie end up eating Christmas Eve dinner?
hint: Famous for the Grand Slam breakfast, and open when the turkey's on fire.
funFact: Scott's sales pitch to a skeptical Charlie: “Everybody likes Denny's. It's an American institution.” Charlie: unconvinced.

question: In Jingle All the Way, a dad races around town on Christmas Eve hunting for which sold-out action figure?
hint: A TV superhero with a jetpack. Every kid wants one. Every store is out.
funFact: The hero's catchphrase is “It's Turbo time!” Also every parent's battle cry on December 23rd.

question: In Jingle All the Way, Howard misses his son Jamie's graduation from what kind of class? (Dad of the Year, folks.)
hint: Think belts, kicks and a dojo. Hi-yah!
funFact: Jamie is played by Jake Lloyd, later young Anakin Skywalker in Star Wars: Episode I. From Turbo-Man fan to future Darth Vader!

question: In Scrooged, Bill Murray's Frank Cross is the youngest president in the history of what kind of company?
hint: His company decides what's on your screen every night. Ultimate remote-control power.
funFact: Bill Murray's real-life brothers Brian Doyle-Murray, John Murray and Joel Murray all appear in the film. Family reunion, Hollywood-style.

question: In Scrooged, what does the Ghost of Christmas Past drive around in?
hint: Yellow, has a meter, and takes you WAY back. Hail it!
funFact: The cab-driving ghost is David Johansen, singer of the New York Dolls. A rock-and-roll ghost with New York driving skills.

question: In Christmas with the Kranks, Luther and Nora plan to skip the holidays entirely and take what kind of trip instead?
hint: Sun, sea, buffet lines and a very big boat.
funFact: Tim Allen and Jamie Lee Curtis play the Kranks. So yes: the star of The Santa Clause tried to skip Christmas.

question: In Jack Frost (1998), Michael Keaton plays a musician dad who comes back to life as… what, exactly?
hint: Carrot nose optional. Below-freezing temperatures NOT optional.
funFact: Michael Keaton also voices Jack in his frosty new form. Beetlejuice, Batman… snowman.

question: Why does Charlie-in-the-Box think no child will ever want him?
answer: His name is Charlie instead of Jack
hint: What's that pop-up toy normally called? His name is… not that.
funFact: He proudly calls himself the island's “official sentry.” Security guard by day, identity crisis by night.

question: Once the Abominable Snow Monster is tamed, what job does he do on Santa's Christmas tree?
accept: Puts the star on the tree
hint: He's tall enough to skip the stepladder. Every family needs one.
funFact: Rudolph's prospector pal brings him back reformed and ready to help. From abominable to adorable in one dental visit.

question: How does Rudolph's elf pal make the Abominable Snow Monster harmless?
answer: He pulls out all its teeth
hint: Think about the elf's dream job. Open wide!
funFact: The elf's career goal, from the very start: “Someday I'd like to be a dentist.” His first patient? A giant snow monster.

question: Which of Santa's famous eight reindeer is Rudolph's dad?
hint: German for “thunder,” and one letter off from the meal you're about to eat.
funFact: Rudolph himself was voiced by a woman, Billie Mae Richards, credited as “Billy Richards.” Talk about a secret identity!

question: Rudolph's prospector pal survives going over a cliff with the Abominable Snow Monster. Finish his explanation: “Didn't I ever tell you about Bumbles? Bumbles…”
hint: It's what a rubber ball does when you drop it. Even off a cliff, apparently.
funFact: Larry D. Mann, who voices the prospector, reportedly recorded the snowman's narration first, before Burl Ives got the gig.

question: The elves proudly sing their brand-new song for Santa. Finish his grumpy review: “Hmm. Well, it…”
hint: Translation: not quite ready for the big show. Ouch, Santa.
funFact: The song they'd rehearsed so hard was “We Are Santa's Elves.” Tough crowd at the North Pole.

question: Rudolph and his elf pal, two runaway outcasts, belt out a duet. What's the song called?
hint: A song about being a pair of oddballs, and proud of it.
funFact: From 1965 it was swapped out for a song called “Fame and Fortune,” and the original wasn't restored until 1998. Misfits for real!

movie: Santa Claus Is Comin' to Town (1970)
question: What simple toy does Kris give the scary Winter Warlock, melting his icy heart?
hint: It runs on tracks and makes a very cheerful noise. All aboard!
funFact: Kris then coaches him with the song “Put One Foot in Front of the Other.” Best villain therapy ever.

movie: Santa Claus Is Comin' to Town (1970)
question: Why does Sombertown's grumpy mayor ban all toys?
answer: He trips over a toy duck
accept: He slipped on a toy duck
hint: It all started with one painful fall… and a quack.
funFact: Kris dodges the ban by sneaking down chimneys and leaving toys in stockings. A legend (and a loophole) is born.

question: Finish Sally's letter to Santa: “Just send money. How about…”
hint: Two kinds of paper bills. She's not greedy, just specific.
funFact: Sally's reasoning: all she wants is what's coming to her, her fair share. Little sister, big negotiator.

question: Finish Linus's line about Charlie Brown's tree: “It's not bad at all, really. Maybe it just needs a little…”
hint: All you need, according to the Beatles.
funFact: As he says it, Linus wraps his beloved security blanket around the tree like a tree skirt. Biggest sacrifice in Peanuts history.

question: Little Cindy Lou Who catches the Grinch stuffing her family's tree up the chimney. What fib does he tell her?
answer: Taking it to his workshop to fix a light that won't light on one side
accept: A light won't light on one side
Taking it to his workshop to fix it
hint: He claims it's just a quick repair job. Totally legit. Very believable.
funFact: Boris Karloff, famous as Frankenstein's monster, voices both the Grinch AND the narrator. He's basically narrating himself.

question: Which Sherlock and Doctor Strange star voices the Grinch in Illumination's 2018 movie?
hint: His first name is also a fancy eggs dish. Hollandaise optional.
funFact: Pharrell Williams narrates the 2018 film. Happy? The Grinch would never.

question: Lock, Shock and Barrel deliver the kidnapped Santa to which bug-filled, burlap-sack villain?
hint: A burlap sack full of bugs who sings a jazzy number while rolling dice.
funFact: He's voiced by Ken Page, who originated Old Deuteronomy in Cats on Broadway. From a cat to a sack of bugs!

question: Sally pours out a magic potion to ground Jack's Christmas Eve sleigh ride. What weather does it create?
hint: The same weather that made Santa need Rudolph in the famous song.
funFact: It nearly works, until Zero's glowing nose lights the way and he's sent “to the head of the team.” Rudolph, check your contract.

question: What word does the conductor punch into the boy's ticket at the very end?
hint: The whole movie in one word. Also the thing the bell needs.
funFact: The girl's ticket says LEAD, and the know-it-all's says LEARN. The Conductor: part-time life coach.

question: Who is the ghostly figure who helps the boy across the roof of the speeding train?
hint: A wandering vagabond who rides the rails. No ticket required.
funFact: He's played by Tom Hanks, who also plays the Conductor, Santa, the boy's dad and the narrator. Busy Christmas!

question: At the high school dance, George and Mary dance until the gym floor opens up. What do they fall into?
hint: Bring your swimsuit. George and Mary did not.
funFact: The pool is real! It's hidden under the gym floor at Beverly Hills High School. Every school dance should have a trapdoor.

question: In the world where George was never born, what has his hometown been renamed?
hint: Named after the town's greediest banker. The welcome sign is NOT welcoming.
funFact: Its snow was a new mix of foamite, soap flakes, water and sugar. Before that, movie snow was often made of cornflakes. Crunchy!

question: George's pals Bert and Ernie share names with two Muppets. Bert is a cop. What does Ernie do for a living?
hint: You'd whistle for him on a busy street. Meter's running!
funFact: Per Sesame Street writer Jerry Juhl, producer Jon Stone said the shared Muppet names were pure coincidence. Suuure.

question: Kris tells a Macy's shopper, “Our skates are very good, but not quite good enough.” Which rival store does he send her to?
hint: A famous New York store starting with G. Macy's archrival!
funFact: He also sends a mom to Schoenfeld's on Lexington Avenue for an $8.50 fire engine. Worst salesman, best Santa.

question: In the 1994 remake, what does little Susan hand the judge that wins the whole case?
answer: A Christmas card with a dollar bill
accept: A dollar bill with “In God We Trust” circled
hint: George Washington's face is involved. So is the motto on the back.
funFact: She circled “In God We Trust”: if the government can trust without proof, so can New York. Case closed!

question: In Home Alone, which actress plays Kevin's mom, Kate, who famously screams “KEVIN!” on the plane?
hint: Before Moira Rose and her wigs on Schitt's Creek, she was the world's most frantic mom.
funFact: Catherine O'Hara also voiced Sally the rag doll in The Nightmare Before Christmas. Two Christmas classics, one legend.

question: What's the title of the black-and-white gangster movie Kevin watches in Home Alone?
hint: The first word is a kind of heavenly being. The rest could use a bath.
funFact: It isn't a real old movie! It was shot just for Home Alone, spoofing the 1938 James Cagney film Angels with Dirty Faces.

question: In Home Alone, Buzz tells Kevin a spooky rumor about their neighbor Old Man Marley. What nickname does Buzz give him?
hint: A city in Indiana, plus a snow-clearing tool. Spooky!
funFact: Marley turns out to be a kind, lonely neighbor who rescues Kevin from the burglars. Buzz: wrong about everything.

movie: Home Alone 2: Lost in New York (1992)
question: In Home Alone 2, what's the name of the handheld tape recorder Kevin uses to fake a grown-up voice?
hint: It TALKS back… and it's made for a kid.
funFact: Tiger Electronics built it as a movie prop, then fans begged for the real thing. It became a must-have for Christmas 1993.

movie: Home Alone 2: Lost in New York (1992)
question: In Home Alone 2, what's the name of the toy store that Harry and Marv plan to rob on Christmas Eve?
hint: Named after its kindly owner, plus a fancy word for a box of treasures.
funFact: Mr. Duncan was donating the store's Christmas proceeds to a children's hospital. Robbing HIM? Harry and Marv, really?

question: In Elf, which Christmas-season duet does Buddy hear Jovie singing in the store's locker-room shower?
hint: A flirty duet about a guest who wants to leave on a snowy night. Brrr.
funFact: Zooey Deschanel, who plays Jovie, really can sing: she later formed the duo She & Him. Buddy has great taste in shower singers.

question: In Elf, which Godfather actor plays Buddy's workaholic dad, Walter Hobbs?
hint: In The Godfather, he played hot-headed Sonny Corleone.
funFact: When we first meet Walter, he's on Santa's naughty list. By the end? Upgraded.

question: In Elf, Buddy mistakes the grumpy children's author Miles Finch for an elf. Which actor plays him?
hint: He later won Emmys as Tyrion Lannister on Game of Thrones.
funFact: Miles warns, “Call me elf one more time!” Buddy's very next line: “He's an angry elf.” It does not go well.

question: In Christmas Vacation, an uninvited houseguest shows up with a very unwilling “present” for Clark, wearing a big bow. Who is the “present”?
hint: He's the guy who cut Clark's Christmas bonus. Big mistake.
funFact: Clark had ranted that he wanted the man brought to him with a big ribbon on his head. His RV-driving in-law took notes.

question: In Christmas Vacation, what are the first names of the Griswolds' snooty yuppie neighbors?
hint: The wife is played by Julia Louis-Dreyfus, Elaine from Seinfeld.
funFact: Their last name is Chester, and they gave us the immortal shouting match: “Why is the carpet all wet, Todd?” “I don't KNOW, Margo!”

question: In Christmas Vacation, which relative says at the dinner table, “Save the neck for me, Clark”?
hint: He shows up uninvited in a rusty RV and parks it in the driveway.
funFact: Randy Quaid first played Cousin Eddie in National Lampoon's Vacation (1983). Some relatives just keep showing up.

question: In A Christmas Story, Ralphie finally decodes Little Orphan Annie's secret message. What does it say?
answer: Be sure to drink your Ovaltine
hint: A plug for the radio show's sponsor, a malted milk drink.
funFact: Ralphie's disgusted verdict: “A crummy commercial?!” Every kid with a decoder pin, betrayed.

question: In A Christmas Story, after the Bumpus hounds devour the turkey, where do the Parkers end up eating Christmas dinner?
hint: They're served a whole roast duck, and it's smiling at them.
funFact: Ralphie remembers it as the Christmas they discovered “Chinese turkey.” Final score: Bumpus hounds 1, Parkers 0.

question: In Die Hard, which actor plays the suave villain Hans Gruber, in his first film role?
hint: He later played Professor Snape. Always.
funFact: Holly McClane goes by her maiden name, Gennero, at work. Hans still finds out who she is, thanks to a nosy TV reporter.

question: In Die Hard, a fellow plane passenger tells McClane to beat jet lag by taking off his shoes and socks and doing what?
accept: Walk barefoot and make fists with his toes
hint: It's done on the carpet, barefoot. Your toes do all the work.
funFact: Taking that advice is why McClane spends the WHOLE adventure barefoot. Worst travel tip ever.

question: In The Santa Clause, what's the first name of Charlie's stepdad, the psychiatrist married to Scott's ex-wife?
hint: He's played by Judge Reinhold. Four letters, rhymes with “kneel.”
funFact: The sarcastic head elf, Bernard, is David Krumholtz, later the star of TV's Numb3rs. Elf management is serious business.

question: In The Santa Clause, finish the card Santa leaves behind: “If something should happen to me, put on my suit…”
answer: The reindeer will know what to do
accept: Reindeer will know what to do
hint: Santa's flying team will take it from there. Trust the antlers.
funFact: That's the fine print, the “Santa Clause”: whoever puts on the suit becomes the new Santa. ALWAYS read the card.

question: In Jingle All the Way, which comedian plays Myron, the frazzled mailman chasing the same toy?
hint: A one-name stand-up comic who shares his name with a legendary sailor.
funFact: Myron later dresses as the superhero's archenemy, Dementor, at the big parade. Mailman by day, supervillain by parade.

question: In Scrooged, the sweet-looking Ghost of Christmas Present wallops Frank with which kitchen appliance?
hint: It makes your bread crispy, and Frank's ears ring.
funFact: Bill Murray insisted Carol Kane hit him for real; in one scene she yanked his lip so hard it tore. Fairy? Yes. Gentle? No.

question: Christmas with the Kranks is based on which John Grisham novel?
hint: The title is exactly what the Kranks plan to do. Spoiler: it doesn't work.
funFact: The screenplay was written by Chris Columbus, director of the first two Home Alone movies. Christmas chaos is his specialty.

question: In Jack Frost (1998), what magic musical instrument helps bring Jack back to his son, Charlie?
hint: Fits in your pocket, and you play it with your breath.
funFact: Jack was the singer and harmonica player of the Jack Frost Band. Some dads never stop touring.

question: The special's stop-motion puppet animation, nicknamed “Animagic,” was filmed in which country?
hint: The Land of the Rising Sun.
funFact: Animator Tadahito Mochinaga supervised the puppet work at a studio in Tokyo. Rudolph: international star.

question: After the 1964 premiere, viewers wrote in about a loose end. What scene was added in 1965 to fix it?
answer: Santa picking up the Misfit Toys
accept: Santa stopping at the Island of Misfit Toys
Santa going back for the Misfit Toys
hint: Rudolph made a promise on that island. Kids wanted it kept!
funFact: The original Rudolph and Santa puppets sold at auction in 2020 for $368,000. Not bad for a misfit.

question: What's the name of the young buck who befriends Rudolph at the Reindeer Games, until he sees Rudolph's glowing nose?
hint: Also the name of a spicy cinnamon candy. Hot stuff!
funFact: Fireball is voiced by Alfie Scopp, who also voices Charlie-in-the-Box. Bully AND misfit: that's range.

question: At the very end, the prospector licks his pickaxe and finally strikes it rich. What has he found?
hint: Think candy canes. Minty fresh!
funFact: His victory cry: “Peppermint! What I've been searching for all my life!” The scene was cut from TV airings for decades. Sorry, Yukon.

movie: Santa Claus Is Comin' to Town (1970)
question: How do Kris's reindeer learn to fly?
answer: They eat the Winter Warlock's magic feed corn
hint: A magical snack from a reformed villain. Breakfast of champions.
funFact: The flying reindeer help Kris and his friends escape from jail. Santa's origin story includes a jailbreak!

question: Finish Lucy's complaint: “Christmas is a big commercial racket. It's run by a big…”
hint: A shadowy organization from back East. Very mysterious. Very Lucy.
funFact: The kids found phrases like “Eastern syndicate” tough to say, and Sally's voice actress was too young to read, so she was fed her lines one at a time.

question: Charles Schulz flatly refused to add something almost every TV cartoon comedy had in 1965. What was it?
hint: Audience reactions that weren't really live. Ha. Ha. Ha.
funFact: CBS execs also hated the slow pace. Then about 45% of the TV audience tuned in on premiere night. Good grief!

question: Which legendary Looney Tunes animator, a co-creator of Wile E. Coyote and the Road Runner, directed the 1966 special?
hint: His first name rhymes with “duck,” and he directed plenty of Daffy.
funFact: He and Dr. Seuss had teamed up years earlier on World War II Army training cartoons starring Private Snafu.

question: Finish the Grinch's schedule: “4:00, wallow in self-pity. 4:30, stare into the abyss. 5:00, solve world hunger…”
hint: He wants zero credit for it. Very humble. Very Grinch.
funFact: The rest of his day: “5:30, jazzercise. 6:30, dinner with me. I can't cancel that again.” Anthony Hopkins narrates the film.

question: Dr. Finkelstein grumbles that Sally has twice this month slipped which poison into his tea so she could run off?
hint: A poisonous plant whose name sounds like an evening shadow. Spooky gardening!
funFact: Sally is a true rag doll: when she leaps from the tower window and falls to pieces, she just stitches herself back together.

question: Guinness World Records calls this the first film made entirely with which moviemaking technique?
hint: Actors wore suits dotted with tiny markers so computers could copy every move.
funFact: Its budget, about $165 million, was the highest ever for an animated feature at the time. That's a LOT of hot chocolate.

question: Clarence, Angel Second Class, carries a copy of which Mark Twain book?
hint: Its hero tricks his friends into whitewashing a fence. Classic hustle.
funFact: He leaves it for George, inscribed: “Remember, no man is a failure who has friends.” Pass the tissues.

question: Macy's wouldn't take part in the 1994 remake. What's the name of the fictional store that hires Kris instead?
hint: Sounds like what naughty kids find in their stockings.
funFact: Richard Attenborough plays Kris. Yes, Jurassic Park's John Hammond. He spared no expense.

question: In Home Alone, Kate hitches a ride home with Gus Polinski, the “Polka King of the Midwest.” What's his band called?
hint: Named after a city in Wisconsin. Polka is not optional.
funFact: John Candy shot all his scenes in about one day and improvised much of his dialogue. Polka legend, speed run.

question: Which composer earned two Oscar nominations for Home Alone's music?
hint: He also scored Star Wars, Jaws and the first Harry Potter films. Dun-dun… dun-dun…
funFact: One nomination was for the carol “Somewhere in My Memory,” with lyrics by Leslie Bricusse. Hum it and watch the room get misty.

movie: Home Alone 2: Lost in New York (1992)
question: In Home Alone 2, what gift does Kevin give the Pigeon Lady in Central Park as a sign of friendship?
hint: A bird ornament from the toy store's tree. The carol gives you two of them.
funFact: The Pigeon Lady is played by Brenda Fricker, an Oscar winner for My Left Foot. The pigeons are honored.

question: In Elf, during his all-night makeover of the store's Santaland, Buddy recreates what famous painting on an Etch A Sketch?
hint: It hangs in the Louvre in Paris and has a very mysterious smile.
funFact: At the North Pole, Buddy's job was building Etch A Sketches, and he finished only 85 in a day, way short of his quota. Clearly an artist.

question: Elf's director also plays the Hobbs family's doctor, who confirms Buddy is Walter's son. Who is he?
hint: He went on to direct Iron Man, and to play Tony Stark's driver, Happy.
funFact: He also voiced the arctic puffin and Mr. Narwhal, uncredited. Director, doctor, puffin: the full Christmas package.

question: In Christmas Vacation, which future Big Bang Theory star plays Clark's son, Rusty?
hint: On The Big Bang Theory, he played Leonard. Bazinga!
funFact: Juliette Lewis plays Rusty's sister, Audrey. Both survive Clark's Christmas, which is the real achievement.

question: Before his wild sled ride in Christmas Vacation, Clark coats the sled with an experimental product his company is working on. What is it?
hint: It's meant for frying pans, not sleds. Results: blazing.
funFact: Clark is going for a new “amateur recreational saucer-sled land-speed record.” Mission accomplished, and then some.

question: In A Christmas Story, Schwartz breaks schoolyard etiquette when he dares Flick. Which step in the order of dares does he skip?
hint: Ralphie's narration says Schwartz went “right for the throat,” skipping a whole rung of the dare ladder.
funFact: Flick stays stuck to the pole until the fire department arrives to free him. Schoolyard etiquette matters, people.

question: In A Christmas Story, what's the name of the yellow-eyed bully who torments Ralphie and his friends?
hint: His sidekick is Grover Dill. First name: four letters, rhymes with “cut.”
funFact: The film is set in fictional Hohman, Indiana, based on writer Jean Shepherd's hometown of Hammond.

question: In Die Hard, Argyle the limo driver plays “Christmas in Hollis.” Which hip-hop group recorded it?
hint: They also teamed up with Aerosmith on “Walk This Way.”
funFact: When McClane grumbles, Argyle insists it IS Christmas music. Argyle: the true hero of Die Hard.

question: In The Santa Clause, Judy the elf's hot cocoa recipe is “Not too hot, extra chocolate…” and what else?
hint: It's how James Bond takes his martini. Licence to chill.
funFact: Judy's boast: “My own recipe. Took me 1,200 years to get it right.” Worth the wait.

question: In Jingle All the Way, what's the name of Turbo-Man's sidekick?
hint: Also the extra rocket that gives a spacecraft its liftoff push.
funFact: At the big parade, Arnold's dad character ends up INSIDE the Turbo-Man suit himself. Best. Dad. Costume. Ever.

question: In Scrooged, which Olympic gymnast plays Tiny Tim in Frank's big live production of A Christmas Carol?
hint: She won all-around gold at the 1984 Los Angeles Olympics. Perfect 10!
funFact: Comedian Buddy Hackett plays Scrooge in the same production. Peak 1980s TV stunt casting.

question: In Christmas with the Kranks, the couple won't put their giant snowman up on the roof. What two-word protest do the neighborhood kids chant?
hint: It names the famous snowman from the song. Justice for snowmen!
funFact: Then daughter Blair announces a surprise visit home from Peru, and the Kranks scramble to throw Christmas together after all.

question: Which famous puppet company created the title character's suit in Jack Frost (1998)?
hint: Founded by the creator of the Muppets. Kermit's family business.
funFact: George Clooney was first set to star, and the snowman was designed to look like him. Fun twist: Clooney and Keaton both played Batman.
